doc.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Oscar Peterson's school, moving to New York in 1961 and the Playboy Club
summary: After Oscar Peterson's school in Toronto he moved to New York with Mike Longo and Jimmy Young, got the Playboy Club gig, and discusses competition for work.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Eventually you went to New York?

Yeah. I went to New York in 1960 — no that’s not right — ‘61. I went up to Oscar Peterson’s School in Toronto in ‘60, I remember turning 21 in a little apartment, on a cold winter night in Toronto on December 6th. All of a sudden I said I’m 21. I bought myself a quart of beer and celebrated. And Mike Longo, the pianist who you may know, he and I had a trio with a drummer named Jimmy Young, and we moved to New York together in April of ‘61. I started working at the Playboy Club and —
Was there pretty fierce competition for gigs like that?

Well I guess there was but we were some pretty capable players at that point, and we were young, we were able to put up with the hours, and somehow we got the gig. And there was lots of musicians working in New York, you know I mean there was plenty of guys. Gee in 1960 it was a very busy period, and still is. It’s still very busy. But we got our jobs, and I could play reasonably well, so when I played with people a lot of them wanted me to play with them again. And that’s the key you know. Somehow they say let’s use that bass player again, the band sounded good, or let’s use that drummer. Somehow if you can get that going, you’re on your way to starving.
You’re well on your way to starving.

You’re well on your way to starving as a musician. You’ve worked those gigs you cannot possibly afford to make a living at. But you know you have to find a way. And that’s the thing about music, you just have to find a way to make a living at it.
